content:
Hi,

I am currently not quite sure what I currently need to work on Std. I have cloned my fork and used to be able to just run make -C build/release -j$(nproc || sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu) whenever I wanted a change to be available in another file (which gave at least a lot of time to think :slight_smile: ).

Now, I had to merge master due to a conflict and this no longer works. I recloned the repo and now notice that I have a button for the build process in VS Code, but afterwards it doesn't know definitions added in imported files. I noticed that there is now a lake file, so I also run lake build, but this fails pretty quickly with

✖ [2/4681] Building Init.Prelude
trace: .> LEAN_PATH=/home/johannes/lean4/build/debug/stage1/lib/lean /home/johannes/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.29.1/bin/lean -Dbackward.do.legacy=false /home/johannes/lean4/src/Init/Prelude.lean -o /home/johannes/lean4/build/debug/stage1/lib/lean/Init/Prelude.olean -i /home/johannes/lean4/build/debug/stage1/lib/lean/Init/Prelude.ilean -c /home/johannes/lean4/build/debug/stage1/lib/temp/Init/Prelude.c --setup /home/johannes/lean4/build/debug/stage1/lib/temp/Init/Prelude.setup.json --json
error: Init/Prelude.lean:3691:11: Unknown attribute `[weak_specialize]`
error: Lean exited with code 1
Some required targets logged failures:
- Init.Prelude
error: build failed

I have tested it both with the debug and release version I can do with cmake. What else is needed? I haven't found anything in the docs in github, but maybe I overlooked something.

make -C build/release -j<something> is what I am using, so the invocation is probably not the issue. It's possible that you merged master at an inopportune time and are missing a stage0 update. Have you tried it with the current master?
Last time was 3 days ago. I try it again now
Can you be more specific what the error is with the make invocation?
So, make runs fine, but when I open a file I get the error posted above, that it cant build Init. Also the branch builds on Github so its not fundamentally broken.
How did you open the lean4 workspace? We switch to opening via Open Folder (like other Lean projects) a while ago.

I have the same exact problem. I think it started with the move away from the "lean4" toolchain.

I thought I did something wrong so did not investigate further.

I just reproduced it from a fresh clone:

$ git clone https://github.com/leanprover/lean4.git
$ cd lean4
$ cmake --preset release
$ make -C build/release -j$(nproc || sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu)
$ code .
# open any file in `src/Lean` click "Restart File" and get the error

Is the last step wrong?

fiforeach said:

I have the same exact problem. I think it started with the move away from the "lean4" toolchain.

Make sure that you have the most recent version of Elan and of the VS Code extension.

Marc Huisinga said:

Make sure that you have the most recent version of Elan and of the VS Code extension.

Updating Elan and recompiling fixed the issue for me, thanks. (Updating Elan was not enough.)
I used the same workflow as fiforeach , but updating elan fixed it for me as well. Thanks
